title: K disagreements trace to foot isolation, borderline loops and target localization
statement: The same two masked model readers reread all7 prior K contexts with an exact target frame,100px expanded context and original TIFF sensitivity for the4 originally disputed cases. Both final7-row outputs were frozen before source-linked analysis; original annotations remain unchanged. The f94v foot disagreement converges to present/present with expanded context. The f103r loop stays round versus unclear; the f105r foot stays unclear versus present, and its upper loop becomes unclear for both. Both reject the specifically marked f41r fragment as a complete K example, but tight localization limits any page-level glyph conclusion. A new f104r disagreement appears over foot-versus-adjacent-letter ink. Exact full-feature agreement remains3/7, and jointly accepted/unambiguous targets fall from6 to5. Both readers judge the4 JPEG/TIFF source pairs geometrically the same. Better context clarifies selected ink boundaries but does not yield a stable exclusive K signature for hand3.

case_findings.interpretation: Readers now both describe an outward projection separated by a visible gap from following-letter ink. This is paired-reader convergence, not expert ground truth.
Compact angular aperture remains near a qualitative category boundary; no calibrated roundness threshold is available.

case_findings.review: unclear/present; both bar bowed and upper loop unclear
case_findings.interpretation: A tiny basal swelling may be a spur or blunt stem ending; source versions do not remove ambiguity. The earlier three-recipe straight-bar pattern does not survive this reread.

Marked detail shows an open hook; the selection may exclude part of a larger compound/two-stem form. Treat as a localization-limited example, not proof that the page lacks K or changes hand attribution.
More context raises the question of membership in the next letter. Retain this newly exposed disagreement rather than dropping the original agreeing control.

check: Validate complete glyph localization with a paleographer before another feature-rate study. Mark the whole glyph with sufficient margin and keep uncertain compound/hook identity separate from K-shape categories. Prospectively define measurable loop roundness and an isolated-foot criterion using known-script examples. Keep original and reread ratings separate and retain uncertain adjacent-stroke ownership; no forced consensus or source-based reassignment.

plan.comparison: Align seven original K contexts by source_index. Retain original ratings. Validate/freeze both7-row review files before opening source-linked results. Compare feature agreement including unclear, jointly accepted/unambiguous contexts, each reader change, and the four originally nonidentical feature cases. Do not combine original/review into independent sample counts. Report same/different JPEG-TIFF assessments. No forced consensus.
plan.causal_limit: Target marking, larger context, optional TIFF and more explicit foot-isolation instruction changed together. A convergence cannot uniquely be assigned to any one intervention.
plan.reader_design: Same two model readers as initial masked annotation; this is followup interpretation, not fresh blind replication or human expert adjudication.
plan.v1_excluded: Layout clipping detected before root read review results; retain v1 but analyze v2 only.

A descending stroke from above reaches the upper area, while the target aperture remains identifiable.

The aperture is angular and borderline between round and oval at this resolution. The right stem ends in a distinct rightward basal wedge, separated from the neighboring letter. original_B.note: The central complete tall form has a short straight connector, an oblong upper loop and a distinct lower right projection.

review_B.note: The exact tall pair is identifiable and its connector dips. The right upper return has an apparent interruption near its upper-right side, so I cannot certify a closed oval loop. A small rightward spur is visible at the lower right stem, especially in the complete lower TIFF panel, before the stem's pointed end. JPEG and TIFF support the same geometry; the TIFF does not resolve the upper contact uncertainty.

original_B.note: Complete central tall paired form shows a short straight cross connection, oval upper loop, and a clear right basal hook.

review_B.note: The marked target has a short nearly straight connector and a closed oblong right upper aperture. The right stem has a clear short rightward basal curl separated from the following letter. Context helps identify the paired form despite trimming of part of the left stroke in the enlarged detail.

review_A.note: The specifically marked dominant stroke is a long stem with an open rightward upper hook. Blank space remains below the hook tip in both source panels, rather than a closed aperture. The left stroke outside the blue frame is not substituted. No outward basal projection of the marked stem is identifiable.

review_B.note: The marked upper form is an open arching hook, with its right tip ending above a broad uninked opening rather than enclosing an upper aperture. The enlarged detail contains only part of the left connection and reaches the lower stem boundary, preventing reliable bar and foot isolation. JPEG and TIFF show the same hook and opening.

layout_correction.reason: Card canvas height780 could clip TIFF target at y480+target height*6; TIFF header y450 could overlay JPEG lower pixels. All reviewed targets are reissued with1100px canvas and separate TIFF header550/image580.
layout_correction.timing: Detected during root layout QA before reading either review response. ReaderA completed v1; readerB was interrupted. Preserve v1 answers, use only newv2 as review result.
layout_correction.additional_exposure: Readers may remember v1; this remains a paired reread, not fresh independent replication.

limitations: Paired reread by the same two model agents, not two new independent observers or human paleographic adjudication. The readers remember previous views.

The first review layout could clip TIFF bottoms and overlap a header with JPEG pixels. It was detected before root read either review result; v1 is preserved but excluded. Both readers reread all7 corrected v2 cards. This extra exposure is documented.
Exact target framing, expanded context, TIFF availability and the more explicit foot-isolation instruction changed together, so a changed rating cannot be causally assigned to only one factor.
TIFF dimensions equal the native JPEG dimensions. Nearest-neighbor zoom magnifies pixels without adding optical resolution. Fine stem/end ownership remains interpretation-limited.
Some target detail frames trim outer strokes even when expanded context displays more ink, especially f41r; do not equate fragment rejection with glyph-family absence in the manuscript.
Only selected prior contexts, no complete glyph census. Physical page/quire confounding and lack of hand5 N controls remain. No handwriting classification accuracy or hidden-page fact is inferred.

reproduction.usage: Decode files_base64 to bytes preserving paths under a fresh root; run python k-disagreements/analyze_review.py to reproduce agreement. All original and final rating files are included with exact bytes; images are unnecessary for metrics. To regenerate review cards, also fetch the pinned original JPEGs from prior PR645 plus TIFF URLs/hashes in tiff-audit.json, arranged at sibling hand3-scans and k-disagreements; run prepare_review.py.
